name: Shipping chokepoints
value: Hormuz closed by IRGC; blockade enforced
summary: Iran's navy says a tanker hit a mine and caught fire in Hormuz on 7 Nov; US disables a blockade runner
state: Iran's navy said an oil tanker hit a mine and caught fire in the eastern Strait of Hormuz on 7 Nov (The New Arab), and US Central Command said it fired on and disabled a cargo ship trying to break its blockade of Iranian ports the same day (RFE/RL). UKMTO reported 11 attacks on commercial vessels in the seven days to 4 Nov, and the Revolutionary Guards say Hormuz stays closed until their conditions are met. Iran makes ending the US port blockade a condition of any deal (Euronews). Traffic remains materially impeded.
for_you: Check FCDO travel advice for the Gulf. Shipping disruption tends to raise freight costs and delay goods over the following weeks.

sources.title: The New Arab — Houthis say they targeted Saudi oil sites, troops and Riyadh airport
RFE/RL — Iran live blog: US forces disable ship seeking to break blockade
Euronews — US launches new targeted strikes on Iran as Trump claims progress in talks

why: Around 30% of seaborne oil and much container trade passes Hormuz, Bab el-Mandeb/Suez, Panama and Malacca; disruption raises prices worldwide.
drivers: Houthi/Iran attacks, war-risk insurance, drought (Panama), naval incidents, piracy.

rubric.alert: Hormuz traffic materially impeded, or any chokepoint closed, or two or more disrupted at once.
rubric.watch: One chokepoint disrupted (attacks, large-scale diversions, draught restrictions).
